reason: The core balance deductions have adequate stated premises, but local repairs are needed for frame-law conditions, cross-frame conservation claims, force-field terminology, and dimensional qualifications in the examples.

findings.reason: Clause (d) calls φ_i(x), with x in the full configuration domain Q⊂R^{3N}, an external single-label force, while post-cm02-interactions defines F_i^ext(t,x_i,v_i); align the terminology or arguments.
Clause 4 replaces the integrated total-force term by ΔP using a balance that holds along motions, but the theorem setup assumes only a C² curve family.
The definition promises transformation laws for quantities about any C¹ reference curve o(t), while clause 3 states the angular-momentum and torque laws only for fixed o.
The Remark overstates conservation across frames: the displayed boost laws contain time-varying P or X terms, so K, E, or angular momentum need not remain constant without further hypotheses.

The Remark says energy conservation in one frame is conservation in every frame using the same potential presentation, but the boost term v·RP(t) can vary and the transferred potential can be time-dependent.
The audit says a conserved quantity transforms to a constant with a different value, but the angular-momentum and energy boost terms can vary with X(t) or P(t).
The example adds c(t)=-t² to an energy-valued potential without a dimensional coefficient or normalized time; specify the units, for example c(t)=-(1 J)(t/(1 s))².
With t in seconds and positions in metres, x₁=t e₂ and x₃=e₂+t e₁ have inconsistent dimensions; introduce explicit length and time scales and carry them through the torque calculations.

The annulus is dimensioned in metres but γ(θ)=(cos θ,sin θ,0) has dimensionless coordinates and is not literally in Q; include a length scale and restore units in the derivative and circulation calculations.
W in o(t)=Wt is undeclared and reuses the work symbol; define it as a velocity and distinguish nonzero perpendicular choices for the claimed nonzero correction.
The page says the moving-origin correction is nonzero although the cited example includes V=0 and permits W=0; qualify this claim for nonzero perpendicular velocities.
